summary: This note is an excerpt from the Wikipedia article on the 1964 Disney film Mary Poppins, covering its production basics and the opening plot. It describes the film as a live-action and animated musical fantasy directed by Robert Stevenson, with Julie Andrews making her feature film debut as the title nanny. The plot excerpt covers Bert's introduction on Cherry Tree Lane and the Banks children's advertisement for a new nanny, which magically floats away after George Banks tears it up.
one_line: Wikipedia excerpt on the 1964 Disney musical fantasy film Mary Poppins, its production and opening plot.
key_facts: Mary Poppins is a 1964 American musical-fantasy film directed by Robert Stevenson and produced by Walt Disney.
The songs for Mary Poppins were written and composed by the Sherman Brothers.
The screenplay for Mary Poppins is by Bill Walsh and Don DaGradi.
The screenplay is loosely based on P.L. Travers's book series Mary Poppins.
The film combines live-action and animation.
Julie Andrews stars in her feature film debut as Mary Poppins.
Dick Van Dyke, David Tomlinson, and Glynis Johns are featured in supporting roles.
The film was shot entirely at the Walt Disney Studios in Burbank, California, using painted London background scenes.
The story is set in Edwardian London in 1910.
Bert performs as a one-man band before directly addressing the audience and touring Cherry Tree Lane.
George Banks learns from Winifred that Katie Nanna has left their service after Jane and Michael ran away again.
Constable Jones returns the children, who were chasing a lost kite.
George Banks advertises for a stern, no-nonsense nanny.
Jane and Michael write their own advertisement for a kinder, sweeter nanny.
George Banks rips up the children's letter and throws the scraps in the fireplace, but the remains float up into the air.
